summary: Alabama Power's first of six planned fire towers above Lake Martin: opened 1939, closed 1980, restored by CRATA and open to the public since 2012.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 prefabricated galvanized steel tower with a small cab; CCC crew built a ranger station and outbuildings at its base
facts.agency: CRATA (title since 2010); NHLR still lists Alabama Power Company

access.note: Restored and opened to the public in June 2012; CRATA runs the tower and trails. The sources read do not say whether the cab is open to climbers.

visit.trail_note: Site just off Youngs Ferry Road outside Dadeville; steep 0.4-mile climb from the parking lot to the tower base; Walker Bynum tower trail total length 1.0 mile.

events.note: NHLR gives 1939 as the build year but its description says the WPA built it in 1938; CRATA credits Alabama Power Company and gives April 10, 1939 as the official opening
Smith Mountain was the first of six towers in the network and the district office of the Alabama Division of Forestry
Alabama Forestry Service closed the tower (CRATA); Weebly dates decommissioning to 1981
Closure year; the sources do not give a date for the last watch
Decommissioning as dated by Weebly; conflicts with CRATA's 1980
CRATA obtained title to the site and tower
Restoration completed and tower opened to the public in June 2012 (Weebly); CRATA says the tower has been restored

Restoration was completed and the tower opened to the public in June 2012; CRATA now runs the tower and trails.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1939 as the build year and says the WPA built it in 1938; CRATA credits Alabama Power Company with the construction and CCC boys with the ranger station, and gives April 10, 1939 as the official opening. The story reports both.
NHLR gives the structure as 82 ft; CRATA says the LS-40 is about 90 ft overall. facts.height_m uses NHLR's 25 m; the story reports both.
CRATA gives 1980 for the closure; Weebly gives 1981 for decommissioning. Both are recorded as events.
NHLR lists Alabama Power Company as administrator; CRATA says it has held title since 2010.

notes_for_editor: Build date and builder conflict (WPA 1938 vs Alabama Power and CCC, opening April 10, 1939). The Weebly page's Dadeville Record item is dated April 13, 1939 and reports the dedication, so the two April dates are consistent rather than contradictory. Height conflict (82 ft vs about 90 ft) and closure year conflict (1980 vs 1981) are both in the story. Current access rests on CRATA's own pages and a June 2012 reopening note; the sources read do not say whether the cab is open to climbers, so visit.climbable is omitted.
